title: In Peppol the acceptance decision survives only as transport metadata, not as a business record
content:
A Peppol Access Point moves the document: it takes a business document from one participant and delivers it to another. When a document is accepted, that acceptance is captured in the same terms as the transfer — as transport metadata attached to a message.

The research's point is that acceptance is a business decision wearing a transport costume. Whether a document was cleared, by whom, and against which rule is a statement about obligations between two parties, not about whether bytes arrived. Recording it as delivery metadata makes it awkward to reason about later, because the record is shaped for a message pipeline rather than for the obligation it creates.

Separating the two is the fit. The clearance decision becomes its own attributed record while the Access Point continues to do transport, which leaves Helger's existing role untouched and adds a layer the transport does not provide. The seam is the moment of acceptance, which is already an explicit step in the flow rather than something that has to be invented.
